subject: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R

messages.author: ca51dc784e0edba6
messages.subject: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R
parts:
Hi,

   I recently used Rstan to load results from cmdstan and I realized that my statistical results are inconsistent even if I used the identical data.

Assume that with cmdstan, I generate n chains with m samples saved as: chain_1.csv, chain_2.csv,... chain_n.csv, and each chain has a parameter x.

Now, I used the following code and the result is always different.

data <- read_stan_csv(c("chain_1.csv", "chain_2.csv", ..., "chain_n.csv");
extract (data, "x")$x[1] # I just want to access the first data.

Intuitively, I thought that "extract (data, "x")$x[1]" is always the same if I used the same data, but actually it was not. Is this an expected behavior? or did I do something wrong?

I would greatly appreciate it if you would answer my question.

messages.subject: Re: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R
parts:
I think I need to clarify what I meant.

If I run the following code, then "extract (data, "x")$x[1]" is the same:

data <- read_stan_csv(c("chain_1.csv", "chain_2.csv", ..., "chain_n.csv");
extract (data, "x")$x[1] # I just want to access the first data.

extract (data, "x")$x[1] # the same as the above

However, if I run the code below, the results are not identical:
data1 <- read_stan_csv(c("chain_1.csv", "chain_2.csv", ..., "chain_n.csv");
data2 <- read_stan_csv(c("chain_1.csv", "chain_2.csv", ..., "chain_n.csv");
x1_data1 <- extract (data1, "x")$x[1] 
x1_data2 <-extract (data2, "x")$x[1] # this is not the same as x1_data1.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R
parts:
The extract() function scrambles the draws by design.
Here's the relevant doc line:

extract(object, pars, permuted = TRUE, inc_warmup = FALSE)

If you want the same results, you need

permuted=FALSE

We debated this behavior long and hard, and I have to
admit I lost the battle. I would not have had permutation
as the default, but Andrew thought it was important so that
users didn't make mistakes like taking the first 500 draws
of four chains --- the default prevents that.

Now I think you can set the PRNG seed in R so that you
get the same behavior each time, but I'm not 100% sure.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: default permute in RStan extract [ was: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R]
parts:
Maybe Andrew will want to respond. He was pretty insistent
that the output be permuted by default to prevent mistakes
in inference that would otherwise be possible if you took
subsequences of the data.

Defaults often present this kind of design tradeoff.
I tend to overspecify arguments in my R code anyway to make it
more readable without knowing the package's defaults.

We're going to rethink some tutorial instructions for R
that will cover this kind of thing---extract() isn't our
only problem in terms of users discovering options.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Question on behavior of read_stan_csv in R
parts:
I'm curious about what's the reason behind the changing the return type based on permuted option.

Value

When permuted = TRUE, this function returns a named list, every element of which is an array representing samples for a parameter merged from all chains. When permuted = FALSE, an array is returned;



Wouldn't it make sense to have the results as a list, but without permutation?
